description: Exploring Adaptation Options for Water Infrastructure at Sea Level is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Manchester-by-the-Sea | Department of Public Works; EPA Creating Resilient Water Utilities Program. In Massachusetts, Manchester-by-the-Sea's wastewater treatment plant is located right on the coast. The town's water utility is working with the EPA's Creating Resilient Water Utilities program to consider its adaptation options. Coverage: Massachusetts (2015). The toolkit gives Massachusetts as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: The town of Manchester-by-the-Sea is a community of just under 6,000 residents located on Cape Ann, Massachusetts, approximately 20 miles northeast of Boston. This coastal community—originally gifted by land grant to the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1629—is now known for its picturesque harbor, beautiful beaches, and restored sea captain’s homes.
